Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. Regression tests: test/test_encounter_slots.py. CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The summon now passes its `slot_name=` to `CreatureCmd.add`, which re-sorts `combat.enemies` by `Encounter.slots.index(...)` exactly as `CombatManager.AddCreature` -> `CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName` does. Re-executed witness in audit/tools/, plus regression tests in test/test_encounter_slots.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_slot_name_not_set. TheObscuraNormal.cs:15 declares Slots => ['illusion','obscura']; GenerateMonsters (:25-28) returns (TheObscura, 'obscura') -- reserving 'illusion' for the Parafright the boss later summons (TheObscura.cs:84: `CreatureCmd.Add<Parafright>(base.CombatState, "illusion")`). THE_OBSCURA_NORMAL (the_obscura.py:115-118) is `Encounter(id='the_obscura_normal', monster_classes=[TheObscura])` -- no slots=, no monster_slots=, so TheObscura's slot_name is never set (stays None, C#'s SlotName is 'obscura'), and the encounter's own `.slots` is () instead of ('illusion','obscura'). This is the SAME family as encounter/mytes' Slots gap, but here it is LIVE: `TheObscura._illusion` (the_obscura.py:94-96) calls `CreatureCmd.add(ctx.hooks, Parafright(ctx.hooks, self._rng))` with no `slot_name` argument, even though `CreatureCmd.add` (cmds.py) explicitly supports one and re-sorts on it -- the exact primitive this call needed and did not use. EXECUTED WITNESS (`py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e4.py obscura-slot`): building THE_OBSCURA_NORMAL and firing the real `_illusion` move body leaves `combat.enemies == [TheObscura, Parafright]`, both with `.slot_name is None`. The game's own machinery (CombatManager.AddCreature, CombatManager.cs:848-851: `if (creature.SlotName != null) SortEnemiesBySlotName()`, plus CombatState.cs:495-501's `Slots.IndexOf` comparator) would put Parafright's slot 'illusion' (index 0) BEFORE TheObscura's 'obscura' (index 1) the instant the summon lands -- i.e. the game's post-summon enemy list is [Parafright, TheObscura], the reverse of what the sim produces. This changes the observable enemy-list ORDER for every reader indexed by list position (the obs vector's per-slot enemy encoding, any 'first enemy' iteration) from the moment the Illusion is summoned onward, matching this batch's brief's 'order divergence is a real bug class here' warning exactly (the ovicopter/inklet family). The actual fix site (adding `slot_name='illusion'` to that one `CreatureCmd.add` call, plus `monster_slots=('obscura',)` on the Encounter) is monster-tier content (the_obscura.py's move body), which this `encounter`-kind record does not own -- flagged for `monster/the_obscura` to pick up; see report.
